copies.headline: Adam Is Just Doing This Again
copies.body: Four weeks, four wins, 152.7 a game — first in the league — and a 40-4 all-play that says none of it is smoke. Luck is +0.4, basically nothing. He scored 164.7, 142.9 and 146.8 over the last three and went 30-3 all-play doing it. The draft already graded out at 89, T-2nd, and the roster still projects for 128 a week, first of 12. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Bucky Irving are the floor, not the ceiling. Week 5 is Peter. Mr. Consistent, defending champ, nothing to pick at.

copies.headline: 1-3 And Nobody Should Believe It
copies.body: Christian is 1-3 and it means nothing. The all-play is 29-15, second of twelve, and the last three weeks he's gone 27-6 in all-play while scoring 137.7, 131.1 and 157.5. Luck sits at -1.6 wins, 11th of twelve, which is the statistical way of saying he's been mugged. He's also absorbed 540.7 points against, the 11th-fewest of twelve. The draft was an 89, tied for second, and CeeDee Lamb, Kittle and Chase Brown are why. Week 5 projects 127 against Leif. The record will fix itself.

copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Finally Looks Like A Plan
copies.body: The Rams pipeline is doing real work — Stafford, Kyren Williams, Puka Nacua, and this roster projects about 125 a week, 2nd of 12. John's at 2-2 with 498.5 points, 4th in scoring, and a 26-18 all-play at 59%, 4th of 12. That's a genuinely good team sitting at .500 because luck is -0.4, roughly fair. The Week 2 81.7 is the only blemish, and he's answered with 121.6 and 135.7. The 80 draft grade, T-9th, has aged better than it deserved. He's still up 6-3 on Peter all-time, and this is the roster that keeps it that way.

copies.headline: Peter's 4-0 Is Real, Barely
copies.body: Peter is 4-0 with a 163.0 in Week 4 and the fewest points against in the league at 350.7, which is the fantasy equivalent of winning the lottery while also being pretty good at math. The scoring is legitimate — 125.3 a game, 27-17 all-play, 3rd of 12 both ways. The draft was legitimate too, 89 out of 100, best in the league. The problem is what's left: this roster projects 107 a week, 12th of 12, with Lamar Jackson questionable and Tee Higgins questionable. Week 5 projects 96 against Adam. The 2022 version wouldn't have needed the luck.

copies.headline: CJ's 3-1 Is Held Together With Burrow
copies.body: CJ is 3-1, which sounds better than 24-20 all-play, 54%, 5th of 12. That's the honest version: a slightly-above-average scorer with +0.8 wins of luck padding the ledger. The 116.3 per game is real enough, but the floor showed up in Week 3 at 97.9. The bigger problem is the receiving room — Parker Washington at 14 is the top projection, which is a sentence nobody wants printed. Jonathan Taylor and Joe Burrow carry this. The roster projects 115 a week, 8th of 12, and John's up Week 5.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 3-1 Is Held Together With Tape
copies.body: Kaleb is 3-1 and nobody should be fooled. The all-play is 21-23, 48%, 7th of 12, and the luck number is +1.1 wins — 2nd-luckiest in the league. That's a 113.2 average dressed up as a contender. The 96.4 in Week 2 still counts, and 132.8 is the ceiling, not the norm. Breece Hall is doubtful, which thins a backfield already leaning on Ashton Jeanty. The draft graded out at 86, T-4th of 12, so the pieces are fine. The results are borrowed. Week 5 projects 113 against Noah.

copies.headline: Lunchbox Drops From 163.5 To 82.8
copies.body: Two weeks ago Leif hung 163.5 and looked like a problem. Then 121.5, then 82.8, and now he's #7 with an L2 and a 23-21 all-play that says "fine" in the flattest voice available. Luck is -0.1, so there's no conspiracy — he just stopped scoring. The talent is real: Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey, Derrick Henry, a roster projecting 117 a week, 4th of 12. The draft grade was 80, 12th of 12, and he's outrun it anyway. Week 5 projects 120 against Christian. Score it.

copies.headline: Nico And Nobody, Four Weeks In
copies.body: Mitchell's 112.3 a week is 8th of 12, his all-play is 19-25, and his luck sits at -0.7 — so no, 1-3 isn't a conspiracy, it's mostly just the scoring. The 73.0 in Week 2 followed by 149.2 in Week 3 is the whole profile: one week he's a contender, the next he's a bye-week fill-in. Jahmyr Gibbs projects 27 and Nico Collins 16, which is a real spine, but Travis Kelce projects zero and Rachaad White and DJ Moore are questionable. 121 projected against Logan in Week 5. Win it.

copies.headline: 2-2 Is Doing Isaac A Favor
copies.body: Isaac is 2-2 and shouldn't be. The all-play record is 13-31 — 30 percent, 11th of 12 — which is the real scoreboard, and 102.7 a game ranks 11th. He's survived on 433.0 points against, 3rd-fewest, plus 0.8 wins of luck above expected, T-3rd-luckiest. The last three weeks: 89.3, 121.1, 110.3. That's the ceiling. The strange part is the roster projects 116 a week, 5th of 12, with Ja'Marr Chase and Javonte Williams. The talent is there; the lineup keeps misplacing it. Week 5 projects 121 against Grant.

copies.headline: Amon-Ra Alone Can't Carry This
copies.body: Grant's 2-2 is a magic trick. The all-play is 16-28, 36%, 10th of 12 — meaning in most weeks against most teams, this is a loss. He's survived on the second-fewest points against in the league and a tidy +0.5 luck cushion. The last three weeks: 115.2, 84.4, 104.4, an 11-22 all-play stretch. Amon-Ra St. Brown projects 20, Jacoby Brissett 19, and Dallas Goedert is doubtful at zero. The roster projects 110 a week, 11th of 12. Week 5 against Isaac is 116 of hope.

copies.headline: Logan's 0-4 Is Half Bad Luck, Half Bad Roster
copies.body: Logan has given up 603.6 points, the fewest-avoided total in the league at 12th of 12, and his luck sits at -1.7 wins — he genuinely has been shot at from a tree every Sunday. That's the defense. The prosecution: 104.8 a game, 10th of 12, with 86.4 and 82.5 in back-to-back weeks and a 10-23 all-play over the last three. An 86 draft night hasn't translated; Jefferson and Jeremiyah Love are both questionable, and 111 projected against Mitchell won't fix 0-4. The dress fits.

copies.headline: Postseason Assassin Is Fighting For January Already
copies.body: Noah's draft night graded 86 out of 100, T-4th in the league, which makes 0-4 and 89.9 points per game feel like a crime scene rather than an accident. The all-play is 7-37 — 16 percent, last in the league — so this isn't bad luck; luck is -0.6, meaning he's actually gotten what he earned. Week 4's 110.5 was the season high, which tells you plenty about weeks one through three. Drake Maye projects 18 and Michael Wilson 17 against Kaleb. The lineup projects 117. The assassin needs a pulse first.

intro: Adam is 4-0 and it isn't a fluke — 152.7 a game, an all-play win rate of 91 percent, and a luck rating of plus-0.4 that says he's barely needed the schedule's help. At the other end, Noah is 0-4 with 89.9 per game and a 16 percent all-play, which means he'd be losing to roughly ten of you every week regardless of who showed up on the other side. The week's real story is Leif, who fell from second to seventh without doing anything catastrophic: 123.5 per game is still fourth-best in the league, but a 46 percent form rating and a 52 percent all-play finally caught up to the reputation. And a word for Christian, 1-3 at second overall — 134.7 a game with a minus-1.6 luck rating is the statistical equivalent of being mugged four times in a row.
